issues.description: URL construction complects three concerns: NEVRA parsing, arch detection, and path templating
issues.detail: The koji path is built by string-splitting the tail of a URL, regex-scanning the whole URL for an arch token, and concatenating a templated path. These are three separable facts (package identity, target arch, repo layout) intertwined into one function. Decompose: parse-NEVRA(url) -> {name, version, release, arch}, then render-koji-path(nevra, base). The arch is already in the NEVRA filename; scanning the whole URL is a second source of truth that can disagree with the first.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url treats the URL as a place to search rather than the NEVRA as a value to read
issues.detail: Every RPM filename ends in .<arch>.rpm. That is the canonical value. Regex-searching the entire URL path for any of four arch tokens is place-oriented thinking: the arch lives wherever it happens to appear in the string. A path like /ppc64le-mirror/.../foo.x86_64.rpm would silently mis-classify. Read the arch from the NEVRA filename suffix, which is the actual fact.

issues.description: Silent None return on arch-miss complects error and success in one channel
issues.detail: When no arch matches, extract_arch_from_url returns None and the caller builds a URL containing the literal string 'None' (".../latest/None/Packages/..."). That is a corrupt value flowing downstream as if it were valid. Either raise, or return a Result the caller must destructure. Don't let a missing fact become a string-shaped fact.

issues.description: koji_url_base is a constant masquerading as a local; the koji layout is a value worth naming
issues.detail: The base URL and the '/latest/{arch}/Packages/<first-letter>/<nevra>' shape are facts about the koji repo layout, not about this function. Lift them to module-level named values (or a small dict describing the layout). Then use_koji_url_only becomes: if coreos-pool, keep; else, render(parse(url), layout). The shape of the data becomes inspectable instead of buried in string concatenation.

issues.description: The race condition and untestable-locally downsides are time-semantics issues the code doesn't make explicit
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges a race between bump-lockfile commit and koji tagging: the URL is a fact about a future state of the world. Nothing in the code marks this. A comment naming the temporal assumption ("this URL is valid only after coreos-koji-tagger processes the merge commit") would make the time model legible to the next reader. Right now the assumption lives only in the PR body.

issues.description: Question that should have been asked first: why are we constructing URLs at all instead of asking koji?
issues.detail: The underlying problem is a DNF5 bug returning the wrong baseurl for secondary arches. The fix synthesizes a URL by convention rather than resolving it. A simpler path may exist: query the coreos-pool repo directly per-arch, or post-process repoquery output using the NEVRA as the lookup key against a known-good repo manifest. Worth a hammock session before locking in path-templating as the long-term shape.

review.summary: COMPLECTED and PLACE-ORIENTED. The patch solves a real DNF5 problem but does so by treating URLs as places to scan and splice rather than as renderings of underlying values (NEVRA + arch + repo layout). The arch is read twice — once by regex over the whole URL, once implicitly from the NEVRA filename — which is two sources of truth that can disagree, and a miss silently produces a corrupt 'None'-shaped URL. The koji path structure is a fact about the world worth naming as data instead of inlining as string concatenation. Most importantly, the deeper question — whether constructing URLs by convention is the right shape at all, vs. resolving them against the coreos-pool repo directly — deserves a hammock before this pattern hardens into the lockfile pipeline.
